orders.title: WO-003 — Register DotLn-Angular in this launchpad: the configuration, class, authority profile and gate, the operator's publication grant, the outward vocabulary and the local clone record, so the first target order can activate (version assigned at activation)
orders.objective:
After this order merges, `main` carries everything a target
order for DotLn-Angular needs to activate, run its gate and publish: a valid
`dotln.config.json` registering `dotln-angular` with its class, authority
profile, profile document, documentation root and gate; an operator grant that
admits `repo.push`, `pr.open` and `pr.thread.resolve` for that repository; an
outward vocabulary the publication lint reads; and, on the operator's machine,
the ignored clone record `worktree start` resolves.

orders.title: WO-005 — Foundation libraries for DotLn-Angular: `core` (the typed environment with its production file replacement and `.env` primer, injection tokens, paths and canonical routes, the base-path token, provider composition), `utils` (the `R` and `RA` namespaces with composition typing and ported specs), `i18n` (Transloco with the house `t` pipe), the test-kit convention through secondary entry points, and the proxy configuration
orders.objective:
`apps/dotln` boots from `provideDotlnCore()`, reads a typed
`EnvironmentConfig` through `EnvironmentConfigToken` with a production
replacement and a `.env` primer, builds every URL from `BasePaths` through the
canonical route builders and `AppBasePathToken`, renders its one page's text
through Transloco's `t` pipe, and imports `R` and `RA` from
`@dotln-angular/utils` with types that compose; every injectable introduced
has a test kit in its library's `testing` entry point and a spec that uses it.

**Observed gap (dated 2026-10-18, target `main` at `bc9133e9`; restated by
the pass that sets the base):** the workspace has no libraries, no
environment type, no i18n and no utilities; `tsconfig.base.json` has no
`@dotln-angular/*` paths. Transloco 8.4.0's pipe is named `transloco`, so the
operator's `'key' | t` form needs a house pipe; Transloco has no typed keys
(the typed-keys lint is a later member). Ramda 0.32.0 ships no types
(`@types/ramda` 0.32.0 re-exports `types-ramda`); Ramda Adjunct 6.1.0 ships
its own types and is BSD-3-Clause.

orders.title: WO-008 — Authentication and permissions for DotLn-Angular, legitimate from the Angular side: `auth` with an OpenID Connect authorization-code-with-PKCE client behind a port, in-memory token handling with single-flight refresh, expiry and invalid-token paths, the auth and permission stores, route and feature permission checks from a declared adjacency list, the mocked identity provider through MSW, and the failure-case matrix in unit and e2e tests

the point is to create a platform, not to prove every
constructible case before filing, and the refutation pass must be made worth

goalReview.goalStandard:
## Goal-aligned decisions

The [sequence](../planning/sequence.md) and selected work order determine
current placement and authority. The mission is the outcome; the critical path
is the dependency route to the next outcome. Useful prerequisite or
risk-reduction work must name the blocked outcome it enables. Process activity,
receipt volume and agent utilization are not progress by themselves. Goal
alignment grants no authority to reorder or expand work. In all phases, the Goal
Alignment and Process Cost procedure lives in the generated role skills
[WO-043, 2026-09-11].

Accuracy takes priority over agreement in every phase. The already-equipped
Correctness over Sycophancy rule applies to operator suggestions and the agent's
own premises equally: challenge unsupported claims, distinguish observation
from inference, state material uncertainty, and correct mistakes when evidence
changes. A confident request or an earlier decision is not proof of correctness.
Record material disagreement and its evidence in the same decision or phase
receipt; do not manufacture dissent or seek approval for ordinary judgment.

| Lens                                  | Decision question                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Policy resistance / fixes that fail   | Will local goals or guards undo one another?                                                              |
| Tragedy of the commons                | Does the solution consume shared compute, context or operator attention without accounting for the total? |
| Drift to low performance              | Does it improve an explicit outcome standard rather than normalize a worse baseline?                      |
| Escalation                            | Will additional process provoke more process or workarounds?                                              |
| Success to the successful             | Are credible alternatives excluded merely because the current mechanism already has investment?           |
| Shifting the burden to the intervenor | Does the solution remove recurring operator rescue or depend on it?                                       |
| Rule beating                          | Can the evidence pass without the intended behavior occurring?                                            |
| Seeking the wrong goal                | Does it advance operator flow and the selected product outcome rather than a proxy?                       |

Naive Interventionism adds the existing system's useful functions, affected
consumers, second-order harm, reversibility and smallest useful probe. NoOp
records what happens if nothing changes, why action or inaction wins, and the
evidence that would reopen the choice. Scale detail to consequence: explain
applicable risks and briefly group immaterial lenses with a reason; do not
manufacture eight repetitive paragraphs for routine edits.

Record evidence of benefit and the risks of intervening in existing behavior;
verification and handoff compare observed outcomes with the promised benefit.
Required legal or release actions retain their existing authority; NoOp is a
considered alternative, not an ambient veto or permission to abandon authorized
work.



Material choices and rationales go in existing phase evidence: per-order
`docs/evidence/WO-NNN/decisions.md` and cited product sections for work-order
decisions; planning dispositions/candidate records for planning choices; the
independent report or refutation receipt for its judgment; retained closeout
evidence for release decisions. The decisions index exposes per-order records.
Reuse and link a current rationale until its assumptions change; do not create
a parallel decision log or an extra approval ritual.


This launchpad is the operator's own DotLn instance. Its purpose is to plan and
run bounded, evidence-gated work orders across the operator's repositories, so
that every change arrives as a pull request the operator reads before it merges,
while the kit itself stays upstream and reaches this fork only through starter
updates. The first workstream is DotLn-Angular, an Nx and Angular monorepo that
serves two outcomes at once: the operator's reference Angular workspace, which a
colleague should recognize as the way the operator builds Angular, and the home
of the DotLn console, the Angular shell that will render DotLn's actor-board
view model. The critical path runs from registering that repository in this
launchpad, through one witnessed target order that scaffolds the workspace, to a
foundation where a feature is added by convention: shared libraries, the
component taxonomy, events and stores, and a legitimate client-side
authentication and permission model. Later workstreams join the same way: one
registration and one planning pass each, with the fork's own machinery changes
cut as self orders beside them.

episode.statement: Independent planning refuter (Entropy Reducer, Contra-Auguste mask, architecture-and-semantics lens) for one DotLn planning pass. Verdict: aligned-with-findings. All six orders, WO-003 to WO-008, are aligned-with-findings with 23 known-issue findings, no observed-failure, no vision-contradiction and no hold. Read in full: the canonical refute prompt and closed result schema that npm run plan -- refute printed, saved verbatim by the parent. It supplies the goal and platform standards, the sequence, the six orders' objectives, Cost lines, criteria and non-goals, the cost table and the three trap observations. Vision, roles and capability table are listed as unavailable. To check kit claims the prompt makes, read at HEAD 7ed97cf. That is one commit past base 498e950, and per git diff --stat the extra commit touches only the planning document, which was not read. Files read: scripts/lib/config.mjs (REPOSITORY_KEYS, validateTargetGate, validateRepositories, validateConfig, loadConfig, targetDocRelative); scripts/lib/authority-grants.mjs (readAuthorityGrantRegistry); packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json (content []); scripts/worktree.mjs (the clone message); scripts/outward-lint.mjs and scripts/lib/outward-lint.mjs (the subject.shape rule); scripts/lib/target-publish.mjs (title lint and gh pr create); scripts/lib/target-worktrees.mjs (targetRecordSources); scripts/lib/target-records.mjs (records commit validation); the usage line of scripts/target-gate.mjs. Searched: KIT-MANIFEST.json for the grants path (absent), grep hits for documentationRoot and effect names under scripts/lib, and scripts/lib/harness.mjs for loadConfig. Listed docs/repositories/ to confirm dotln-angular.md exists, without reading its content. Ran two throwaway probes in the scratchpad, since deleted: one shows zsh aborting unquoted --include=*.ts greps, the other shows how this machine's grep (ugrep 7.8.4) handles -rL with no file operand. Did not read docs/planning/angular-workstream-2026-10-18.md, docs/planning/refutations/, docs/lineage/idea-ledger.md, any earlier judgment, or docs/control/local/. Made no repository writes and ran no mutating Git commands; git status stays clean. Spawned no agents and committed no receipt. Findings rely on general knowledge of Nx, MSW, axe-core, OIDC browser clients and the MIT and BSD-3-Clause licenses where marked; none was checked against installed packages. The session system context names the model claude-opus-5-5. Effort has no host readback here and is not reported.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the first step of the critical path as the goal standard states it, 'registering that repository in this launchpad'. Without a dotln.config.json registration (class, authority profile, profile document, documentation root, gate), an operator grant for repo.push, pr.open and pr.thread.resolve, an outward vocabulary and a clone record, no DotLn-Angular target order can activate, run target-gate or publish, so WO-004 to WO-008 are all blocked. NoOp cost in the records: the cost-table row for WO-003 has metrics null and the instance declares no critical-path document ('unavailable: docs/planning/critical-path-2026-09-08.md'), so the records put no number on NoOp. Structurally, NoOp stalls the whole horizon. Doing nothing does not win here. Per the repository contract, planning branches refuse writes outside docs/ and root Markdown, so a root JSON file and packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json can only change through an order or an override. The order is the route that keeps the operator's pull-request read.
orders.systemTraps: Seeking the wrong goal: the only machinery-share observation is WO-001 at 0.649 (no worsening, reopenCandidate false). WO-003's code change is about 3 KB of configuration, set against 1 to 2 hours of executor work plus the full fixed cycle (activation, verification, final review, release close), so its machinery share will probably be at or above that baseline. This is something to watch, not a failure (finding). Rule beating: criterion:2 checks the text of a grant the executor writes itself, so grantedBy 'operator' can pass without any operator act (finding). Shifting the burden: the operator's grant, the clone on the operator's machine and the PR read are acts only the operator can perform, not rescue. WO-001 recorded 4 directions (1 scope expansion, 2 resume directions, 1 resume scope expansion) and had no corrections source, so there is no trend. Drift to low performance: cold-start bytes rose 152 for every role against the previous edition, with no ceiling set (verdict unset). WO-003 edits no skill or contract file and adds nothing to that series. Policy resistance: the new outward vocabulary becomes the publication lint's input, and WO-004's title workflow later rewrites titles into a shape that lint refuses (recorded under WO-004). Tragedy of the commons (about 40 KB of context, one fixed cycle) and escalation (no command or gate added) are immaterial. Success to the successful: the kit's own configuration is the only admitted registration route, so no credible alternative is excluded.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line removes nothing ('the launchpad has no registration today'). It adds dotln.config.json (about 2 KB), one grant (about 0.4 KB), outward-vocabulary.json (about 0.3 KB), an ignored clone record and evidence. Going from unregistered to registered cannot remove more than it adds. The additions are the minimum the kit's loaders require: scripts/lib/config.mjs validates baseBranch, worktreeParent, repositoryClass, profile, gate and documentationRoot, and scripts/outward-lint.mjs throws when the vocabulary is missing. No removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: Mostly yes, and it fails closed where it should (read in scripts/lib/config.mjs). An absent dotln.config.json returns today's defaults (absentConfig, default roots), and a config that omits roots resolves the default document layout, so deleting the file restores the old behavior. A malformed file refuses by path for every loadConfig caller, which would halt the control plane. criterion:1, however, requires npm run resume -- status --json to exit 0 in the order's gate, so a malformed file cannot reach main through the gate. A malformed grant throws in readAuthorityGrantRegistry and a missing vocabulary throws in checkOutwardArtifact. Both refuse outward publication only, which is the correct direction for outward effects. A missing clone record refuses target worktree start and leaves self orders untouched.

findings.reason: criterion:2 checks only the registry's text. packages/skeleton/loadouts/grants.json is instance-owned (absent from KIT-MANIFEST.json, currently []) and admits grantedBy 'operator'. The executor writes that entry, so the evidence passes whether or not the operator authorized these three effects. The operator's pull-request read is the only authority check, and nothing asks the evidence to show the authorization. Separately, readAuthorityGrantRegistry also merges the ignored docs/control/local/authority-grants.json (host-policy grants), so 'prints exactly one grant' also depends on an ignored file that is specific to one machine.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-003's decisions.md or evidence README names no operator dispatch that authorizes exactly repo.push, pr.open and pr.thread.resolve for dotln-angular, or the recorded output of criterion:2 contains a host-policy row from the local registry.

findings.reason: Process cost against a small change: about 3 KB of configuration pays the full fixed cycle, including the full npm test and test:docs gate of criterion:6. The only machinery-share observation is WO-001 at 0.649. elapsedPerCodeByte is null, so there is no baseline for a change the size of a registration. This is to watch, not an observed failure: the trap lists no worsening and reopenCandidate is false.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-003's closed cost-table row records machineryShare above 0.649 and the seeking-the-wrong-goal trap lists WO-003 under worsening or sets reopenCandidate true.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the second stated step, 'one witnessed target order that scaffolds the workspace'. Every later order (WO-005 libraries, WO-006 taxonomy, WO-007 stores, WO-008 authentication) needs the Nx workspace, the tag constraints, the declared gate commands and CI to exist. It is also the first end-to-end run of the target lane on this instance: activation, target-gate, records commit and publication. NoOp cost in the records: the WO-004 row's metrics are null and no critical-path document is declared, so the cost is unrecorded. Structurally, NoOp stalls the horizon and leaves the WO-003 registration unused.
orders.systemTraps: Policy resistance: two title rules meet on one artifact. scripts/lib/outward-lint.mjs refuses any pr-title or commit subject that does not have the shape 'type(scope)?!?: subject' (rule subject.shape). The target's pr-title.yml rewrites the live title to ':sparkles: <type>: ...', and a squash merge then carries that title onto target main. The type list is also declared in two places (finding). A second meeting point: DotLn commits its records under docs/dotln in the target after the gate has run, and the new CI format check covers those files (finding). Rule beating: how the criterion:3 fixture exercises the boundary rule (finding). criterion:6 accepts 'blocked' with the GitHub setting named, an honest escape that records why the behavior did not occur. Shifting the burden: criterion:6 may need the operator to change a GitHub setting. The order records that need instead of depending on a rescue. Tragedy of the commons: one npm ci, one Playwright browser install and the first gate runs dominate the 3 to 5 hours. Context is about 25 KB plus generator help output, and the order pays both the target gate and test:docs in the launchpad order worktree. Escalation: five target scripts mirror the gate, which adds no launchpad process. Drift to low performance: restating the house rules by number in conventions.md keeps the standard explicit. Seeking the wrong goal: the scaffold is the outcome's first concrete artifact, and its machinery share is unknown until run. Success to the successful: Nx, Vitest and Playwright are the operator's declared stack, and no alternative is excluded because of existing investment alone.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes the generator's nx-welcome component and the placeholders, and adds about 60 files, two workflows, two documentation roots and package-lock.json. On an empty target the addition is the deliverable, so no removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: Yes at the order level. A failing target-gate leaves target main untouched (the old behavior) and nothing is published. If the title workflow fails, the title stays as DotLn published it, and criterion:6 records 'blocked' instead of refusing the order. Inside the workspace, @nx/enforce-module-boundaries fails closed by design, which is the intended refusal. The order does not cover one failure: the records commit made after the gate. A CI failure there happens after the gate has passed, on files the order cannot reformat, because validateTargetRecordsCommit rechecks the hash of every recorded blob.

findings.reason: After a passing final review, the kit commits the order file, decisions.md and the verification and final-review reports into the target under the registered documentationRoot (docs/dotln). This is a single-parent records commit, and validateTargetRecordsCommit rechecks every recorded blob. The criterion:7 gate runs on the reviewed commit, before that records commit exists. The CI that criterion:5 requires, however, runs a format check on the pull-request head, which includes docs/dotln. If Prettier would format those launchpad-authored files differently from their recorded bytes, the target PR's CI fails on files the order cannot change. No criterion requires a .prettierignore entry or an equivalent CI exclusion for docs/dotln.
findings.reopenWhen: The CI format check on any DotLn-Angular pull request reports a file under docs/dotln/, or the merged WO-004 workspace has no Prettier or CI exclusion that covers docs/dotln.

findings.reason: scripts/lib/outward-lint.mjs lints DotLn's commit and pr-title subjects against the shape 'type(scope)?!?: subject' and refuses any other shape as subject.shape. WO-003 criterion:3 itself exercises that refusal. pr-title.yml then rewrites the live title to ':sparkles: <type>: ...', and a squash merge uses that title as the commit subject on target main, so the target's history carries subjects the kit's own lint refuses. The type list is also declared twice, as the types in docs/control/outward-vocabulary.json in the launchpad and in .github/gitmoji-map.json in the target, and no criterion asserts that they agree. A type DotLn admits can therefore reach a workflow that has no gitmoji for it. Today target publication lints only the title it sends and does not re-read the live title (scripts/lib/target-publish.mjs), so nothing refuses yet. This conflict can be constructed but has not been observed.
findings.reopenWhen: A DotLn step (re-publication, release close or a later order's commit lint) refuses subject.shape on a DotLn-Angular title or merged subject, or a type in docs/control/outward-vocabulary.json has no entry in .github/gitmoji-map.json.

findings.reason: @nx/enforce-module-boundaries looks up the importing file's project in the project graph and reports nothing for a file that belongs to no project. A fixture inside a linted project, on the other hand, also fails the ordinary lint of criterion:2. tools/lint-fixtures/boundary-violation.spec.ts therefore has to sit in a tagged project whose normal lint excludes it, and lint:fixtures has to check for the rule id rather than for a nonzero exit. Otherwise lint:fixtures can exit 0 on a parse error, a configuration error or another rule's failure while the boundary rule never fires.
findings.reopenWhen: The recorded lint:fixtures output for boundary-violation.spec.ts does not name @nx/enforce-module-boundaries, or npx nx run-many -t lint reports a file under tools/lint-fixtures/.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the first foundation step, 'shared libraries'. WO-006 builds its routes from BasePaths and AppBasePathToken and renders text through the t pipe. WO-007 builds its interceptors on the typed environment, and WO-008 extends core with routePermissions. NoOp cost in the records: the row's metrics are null and no critical-path document is declared. Structurally, NoOp leaves the taxonomy, the stores and authentication each to invent their own environment, token and URL conventions, which defeats 'a feature is added by convention'.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating dominates. The token grep in criterion:2, the literal-text grep in criterion:4 and the TestKit grep in criterion:5 can each pass without the behavior they name. Under the operator's zsh, the unquoted --include patterns empty criterion:4 (a false pass) and break criterion:5 (a false failure) (findings). Seeking the wrong goal: the ported upstream specs test library behavior inside the workspace. They earn their cost only as characterization tests for upgrades, and they bring a licensing duty (finding). Shifting the burden: the .env primer adds a recurring developer step. The declared gate runs e2e in a fresh worktree without .env, so the unprimed path is exercised at merge time. Escalation: two lint rules with fixtures and two commands (env:prime, i18n:check) join the target. Each one is the convention it enforces, not launchpad process. Tragedy of the commons: about 80 KB of context and five new dependencies, a moderate cost. Policy resistance: the token-name and #private rules are local guards that do not conflict with the WO-004 boundary constraints. Drift to low performance and success to the successful: Ramda, Ramda Adjunct and Transloco are the operator's declared house stack, and the observed-gap paragraph records their typing and licensing facts instead of accepting a weaker baseline.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes the placeholder page's inline strings (moved to en.json). It adds three libraries with testing entry points, the environment files, a primer, the proxy configuration, lint rules, about 40 source files and five dependencies. This is product construction, so no removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: Partly. A failing gate leaves target main unchanged. Inside the product, the primer's failure mode is unspecified. criterion:3 builds only after cp .env.example .env, so outside the gate's e2e serve path nothing observes whether a fresh clone without .env falls back to committed defaults or refuses. The test-kit fallback (@dotln-angular/<lib>-testing paths when secondary entry points do not resolve) is an explicit way to degrade, recorded rather than refused. The proxy configuration has no criterion at all, so a failure there would go unnoticed (finding).

findings.reason: criterion:6 ports upstream Ramda (MIT) and Ramda Adjunct (BSD-3-Clause, per the order's own observed gap) specs into libs/shared/utils/src/lib/upstream-specs/, and asks only for 'an attribution comment naming the upstream file'. Both licenses require copies of substantial portions to keep the copyright notice and the license text, and BSD-3-Clause adds the disclaimer. A comment that names a file does not meet that requirement. Under the Clean Room floor, the owner may publish this code only on the licenses' terms, so the criterion as written can pass with copies that do not comply.
findings.reopenWhen: A ported spec under upstream-specs/ neither carries the upstream copyright line and license text nor references a committed third-party notice file that does.

findings.reason: The grep pattern 'new InjectionToken<[^>]*>(' followed by a quoted name matches only one-line declarations whose type argument contains no '>'. A nested generic such as InjectionToken<Record<string, string>> does not match, and neither does any declaration Prettier wraps across lines. For those, grep -vc prints 0 whatever the token is named. The token-name lint rule is the real control, and its fixtures are only required to fail one case.
findings.reopenWhen: A token declared with a nested generic type argument, or across lines, without the dotln-angular. prefix passes both the grep and the lint, or the token-name rule has no fixture for those forms.

findings.reason: Two gaps. (1) In the second command, --include=*.html and --include=*.ts are unquoted. In zsh, the operator's shell on this Darwin machine, an unmatched glob aborts the command with 'no matches found'. The pipe then feeds nothing to wc -l, which prints 0 whatever the templates contain, a false pass. The same unquoted pattern in the inner $(grep ... --include=*.spec.ts) of criterion:5 leaves the outer grep -rL with no file operand. The outer grep then searches whatever its implementation defaults to: here, ugrep 7.8.4 listed standard input and the working directory, a false failure. The kit's hook diagnostic softens this in Claude sessions only. (2) The literal-text pattern works line by line. A text node on its own line between tags, the layout Prettier produces for long content, is never seen, while TypeScript generics such as 'Signal<Foo> = signal<' match falsely.
findings.reopenWhen: A verification of WO-005 runs criterion:4 or criterion:5 under zsh with the --include patterns unquoted, or a template whose literal text sits on its own line passes the check.

findings.reason: The TestKit check lists the specs that call TestBed.configureTestingModule and do not contain the string 'TestKit' anywhere. A spec that imports a kit but still provides the real injectable directly passes. Specs that set up injection another way (TestBed.inject without configureTestingModule, or Injector.create) are never examined.
findings.reopenWhen: A spec under libs/shared provides an injectable through providers: [RealService] or useClass while importing a provide*TestKit, and the check prints nothing.

findings.reason: The title and the Cost line both deliver 'the proxy configuration', but no criterion observes it. criterion:3 covers only the environment files, the primer and two builds. The proxy configuration can be missing, or present but not wired to the serve target, while every criterion passes.
findings.reopenWhen: The merged WO-005 dotln serve target references no proxy configuration, or a development request to the configured API path is not proxied.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the 'component taxonomy' step. WO-007 replaces HomeFacade's static data and has containers dispatch UI events, which assumes the container, facade and mapper split this order creates. NoOp cost in the records: metrics null and no critical-path document. Structurally, NoOp lands the stores without a component taxonomy enforced by location, and leaves 'added by convention' without its main convention. The order also depends on an operator decision, the vendor, that it does not itself produce.
orders.systemTraps: Shifting the burden: the operator must confirm a UI vendor before criterion:1 can be evaluated, and the order names no path for a deferred decision (finding). Rule beating: the axe tag list omits wcag21a and wcag21aa, so rules introduced in WCAG 2.1 never run while the e2e passes (finding). The unquoted --include patterns empty criterion:1 under zsh, and an empty listing satisfies 'lists only files under wrappers' (finding). Lint overrides keyed on location apply only to fixtures whose paths match the override globs, so the fixtures must mirror the fragments, templates, composites and layouts paths. The 'fail its rule' wording in criterion:1 correctly asks for the rule, not just a nonzero exit. Tragedy of the commons: about 120 KB of context and about 60 source files in one PR the operator reads before merge. Operator attention is the shared resource here, and nobody measures it. Escalation: lint:fixtures gains cases and lint:components is added, both product conventions rather than launchpad process. Policy resistance: the no-inject rule for fragments, templates, composites and layouts can collide with the focus management the skip-link keyboard test of criterion:5 needs, so a container or a directive must own the focus logic. Seeking the wrong goal, drift and success to the successful: the taxonomy is the outcome's named convention, and the vendor choice stays with the operator instead of following existing investment.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes the WO-004 placeholder page. It adds the ui, shell and home libraries, lint overrides, a vendor dependency, @axe-core/playwright, about 60 source files and the taxonomy documents. This is product construction, so no removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: At the order level, a failing gate leaves target main unchanged. The vendor dependency is the one place the order refuses instead of degrading. With no operator-confirmed vendor, the '<vendor package>' placeholder in criterion:1 cannot be resolved, and the order names no fallback, such as wrappers over native elements or deferring the wrappers (finding). Lint refusals by location are the intended fail-closed behavior.

findings.reason: AxeBuilder.withTags(['wcag2a','wcag2aa','wcag22aa']) runs only the rules that carry one of those tags. axe-core tags the rules introduced in WCAG 2.1 as wcag21a or wcag21aa (autocomplete-valid and css-orientation-lock, for example), so those rules never run. The criterion therefore passes without any WCAG 2.1 AA check, even though its tag set implies 2.2 AA.
findings.reopenWhen: The committed AxeBuilder call's tag list lacks wcag21a and wcag21aa, or the recorded axe results show no evaluated rule tagged wcag21a or wcag21aa.

findings.reason: criterion:1 depends on a vendor package recorded in docs/evidence/WO-006/decisions.md, and the title says 'operator-confirmed vendor'. WO-004's non-goals leave that decision with the operator. If the operator has not confirmed a vendor when WO-006 is selected, the criterion cannot be evaluated. The order names neither a fallback nor a split (taxonomy now, wrappers later), so the critical path stalls on an operator decision instead of degrading.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-006 is selected or activated while decisions.md records no vendor confirmed by an operator dispatch.

findings.reason: The --include=*.ts in criterion:1 and the two in criterion:2 are unquoted. Under zsh, criterion:1's grep prints nothing, which trivially satisfies 'lists only files under **/wrappers/**', a false pass. criterion:2's first grep prints nothing (a false pass). Its inner substitution comes out empty, so grep -rL gets no file operand and falls back to its implementation's default search, a false failure. The kit's hook diagnostic softens this in Claude sessions only.
findings.reopenWhen: A verification of WO-006 runs criterion:1 or criterion:2 under zsh with the --include patterns unquoted, or a vendor import outside wrappers survives a recorded criterion:1 pass.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the 'events and stores' step. WO-008's authHttpEvents and sessionEvents groups, its single-flight refresh on a 401, the identity provider mocked through MSW and the error and navigation stores all build on this order's events library, interceptors, MSW setup and app-tier stores. NoOp cost in the records: metrics null and no critical-path document. Structurally, NoOp leaves authentication to invent its own event and HTTP plumbing, which breaks the one-way flow that the operator's rule 16 describes.
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating: criterion:4 greps for the option name onUnhandledFrame and for the string environment.mocks instead of observing the behavior (findings). The unquoted --include patterns in criterion:1 and criterion:3 empty those checks under zsh (finding). The hygiene fixtures in criterion:2, each required to exit nonzero, are the strong form. Policy resistance: a query-parameter flag override (?ff=<flag>:on) conflicts with WO-008's permission model if production builds honor it (finding). Tragedy of the commons: about 150 KB of context, about 70 source files and three dependencies in one PR the operator reads, the largest review burden so far. Escalation: lint:hygiene and msw:init join the target as product conventions. Shifting the burden: the MSW handlers keep development independent of a backend and need no operator step. Seeking the wrong goal: the e2e checks tiles, a forced failure, a flag and a canonical navigation, which are outcome behaviors rather than proxies. Drift and success to the successful: NgRx SignalStore with the Events plugin is the declared stack, and the 'or a house withCallState' clause keeps an alternative open.
orders.removalBalance: No. It removes HomeFacade's static data. It adds four libraries, the MSW worker and handlers, the interceptors, a hygiene script, about 70 source files and three dependencies. This is product construction, so no removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: At the order level, yes. In the product, the interceptors turn timeouts and HTTP errors into failure events and the shell shows the error store, so a failing backend degrades to the empty state and a toast (criterion:5) instead of a crash. That is the right degradation. The mock layer's own failure modes are not observed. Unhandled requests may only warn if the option name does not exist in the installed MSW, and nothing checks the production build for MSW code (findings).

findings.reason: MSW 2.x documents the listen option as onUnhandledRequest. onUnhandledFrame works only if the installed major provides it, and the order pins no msw major. Vitest does not type-check by default, so an unknown option is ignored and unhandled requests fall back to the default warning. The grep-based criterion still passes.
findings.reopenWhen: The listen options type of the installed msw setupServer has no onUnhandledFrame, or a spec that issues a request no handler matches passes.

findings.reason: criterion:4 checks that main.ts mentions environment.mocks. It does not check that the production build excludes MSW. A static import of ./mocks/browser ships setupWorker and every handler in the production bundle even when the worker never starts. public/mockServiceWorker.js is also copied into every build output.
findings.reopenWhen: After npx nx build dotln --configuration=production, a search of dist/apps/dotln/browser finds setupWorker or the endpoint path of a mocked handler.

findings.reason: criterion:5 requires ?ff=<flag>:on to change a flagged element, and nothing says whether production builds honor the override. If they do, any visitor can turn on unfinished or permission-adjacent features from the URL. That undercuts WO-008's promise that a visitor 'sees only the routes and features the declared permission model grants'.
findings.reopenWhen: The production build applies a ?ff= query override, or the feature-flag store has no environment switch for URL overrides.

findings.reason: criterion:1 (grep -rl "eventGroup(" ... --include=*.ts | ...) and criterion:3 (grep -rc "withEffects" ... --include=*.ts | grep -v ":0") both require that nothing be printed. Under zsh, the unquoted pattern aborts the first command with 'no matches found' and the pipeline prints nothing, so both pass even with a violation present. The scratch probe reproduced exactly the criterion:3 form. The kit's hook diagnostic softens this in Claude sessions only.
findings.reopenWhen: A verification of WO-007 runs criterion:1 or criterion:3 under zsh with the --include pattern unquoted.

orders.criticalPathAndNoOp: Unblocks the last stated foundation step, 'a legitimate client-side authentication and permission model', and closes the horizon. NoOp cost in the records: metrics null and no critical-path document. Structurally, NoOp leaves the console shell with no identity or permission seam before it renders actor-board data. However, no order in the horizon observes the critical path's stated endpoint, 'a foundation where a feature is added by convention', because every order excludes a second feature (finding).
orders.systemTraps: Rule beating is the main risk. criterion:1 greps house source for localStorage and sessionStorage, while the default stores of an OpenID Connect client library can persist tokens without house code ever naming them (finding). criterion:5 proves only that the string 'mock-idp' is absent from a minified bundle (finding). The unquoted --include patterns in criterion:1 empty that check under zsh (finding). Seeking the wrong goal: this is the horizon's last step, yet the stated outcome, a feature added by convention, is never observed (finding). 'Legitimate' also needs the docs to say that client-side permission checks only affect presentation (finding). Policy resistance: in-memory tokens and the ban on web storage meet the authorization-code redirect, which leaves the page. State and the code_verifier must survive a navigation that the mock may never perform (finding). Tragedy of the commons: 8 to 12 hours, about 160 KB of context and about 60 files make this the largest order, and operator review is the shared cost. Escalation: no new commands, and the failure matrix is product tests. Shifting the burden and drift: the provider swap is meant to be configuration-only, which spares the operator later rework if it holds. Success to the successful: 'one OpenID Connect client library' is left open, so no alternative is excluded because of existing investment.
orders.removalBalance: No. The Cost line removes nothing. It adds the auth library and its kit, the mock provider handlers and a development signing key, two event groups, guards, a permission directive, two routes, about 60 source files and two dependencies. This is product construction, so no removal finding is raised.
orders.failureBehavior: Deliberately no, and correctly so. For authentication the old behavior (no session) is not a safe fallback, so refresh failure and invalid tokens sign the user out and denied routes redirect to /denied. Refusing is the right direction here. At the order level, a failing gate leaves target main unchanged. The degradation to watch is the provider swap. If the mock never performs a top-level redirect, a real provider's redirect can lose the in-memory state and send every sign-in down the state-mismatch path (finding).

findings.reason: criterion:1 greps libs/shared/auth/src and apps/dotln/src for localStorage and sessionStorage. Where tokens actually live is decided by the chosen OpenID Connect client library, and common browser clients default their user or state stores to Web Storage unless configured with an in-memory store. A library default can therefore persist tokens while house code never names storage, and the grep passes.
findings.reopenWhen: After the e2e sign-in, the page's localStorage or sessionStorage contains an access_token, refresh_token or id_token value.

findings.reason: The authorization-code flow sends the browser to the authorize endpoint with a top-level navigation. MSW's service worker bypasses navigation requests (request mode 'navigate'). The mocked provider can therefore answer the token, JWKS and discovery fetches but not the authorize redirect, and in-memory state and the code_verifier do not survive a full-page navigation. Because criterion:1 forbids web storage in house code, the e2e sign-in can pass only in one of two ways: through an in-app mock route that never leaves the SPA, or through a library that persists the state itself. In the first case, the claim that 'swapping the mocked provider for a real one changes configuration and nothing in the Angular code' is never exercised.
findings.reopenWhen: The recorded e2e sign-in completes without a top-level navigation away from the app's origin, or a sign-in against a real-provider configuration ends on the state-mismatch path.

findings.reason: grep -rc "mock-idp" over a minified production bundle proves only that the string is absent. Module paths and identifiers do not survive minification, so mock handlers and the development signing key can ship without the string appearing.
findings.reopenWhen: The production bundle contains the mock signing key's kid or private JWK members, or the endpoint path of a mocked identity provider, or the production build's stats list a mock-provider module.

findings.reason: The goal calls for a legitimate client-side permission model, and with no real API the order makes the route guards and *dotlnHasPermission the whole permission surface. criterion:6 asks authentication.md for the storage rule, the refresh rule, the matrix and the provider swap. It does not ask for the boundary: client-side checks only hide UI, and the API must enforce authorization. A colleague reading the reference workspace could take the guards for the security control.
findings.reopenWhen: docs/dev-reference/security/authentication.md or docs/ai-reference/auth-rules.md does not state that the server enforces authorization and that route and element permission checks only affect presentation.

findings.reason: The goal standard's critical path ends at 'a foundation where a feature is added by convention', and the horizon records no deferrals. Every target order (WO-004 to WO-008) lists 'a second feature' or 'a second app' as a non-goal, and no criterion observes a feature being added by following the conventions. The horizon can therefore close with every part built and the outcome itself unobserved: the seeking-the-wrong-goal pattern of building parts as a proxy for the outcome.
findings.reopenWhen: WO-008 merges, and the next planning pass selects no order whose criteria add a second feature by following docs/dev-reference and docs/ai-reference (or a generator) without editing the shared libraries.

findings.reason: Both greps in criterion:1 use an unquoted --include=*.ts and require that nothing be printed. Under zsh, both commands abort with 'no matches found' and print nothing, so the check passes even with a violation present. The scratch probe reproduced this form. The kit's hook diagnostic softens this in Claude sessions only.
findings.reopenWhen: A verification of WO-008 runs criterion:1 under zsh with the --include patterns unquoted.
